Lee W.: hey @people-ops :wave: i need to request an ADA accommodation — i've been having recurring autoimmune flares and my doc recommended a temporary flexible schedule + some remote days while we get treatment stabilized. can someone advise on next steps?
Olivia (People Ops): Hi Lee — thanks for flagging this. can you share the doctor's note (DM or upload here) and a proposed start date + duration? we can kick off the formal accommodation process once we have that.
Lee W.: attaching the note via DM now. proposed start: next monday (2026-11-01). hoping for 2 remote days/week + flexible start/end times for ~12 weeks. oncall is the trickiest part for me.
peopleops-bot: Submitted medical doc received and assigned case ID PO-20261101-42. An HR specialist will follow up within 2 business days.
Samir R. (Manager): Lee — i support this and appreciate you flagging early. main concern is coverage for critical oncall windows and weekly syncs. happy to adjust team schedule temporarily.
Tara P.: quick q — will this impact any PTO/short-term disability? Lee, if you want, we can also evaluate STD if recovery is expected to exceed company thresholds.
Lee W.: thanks Samir & Tara. i don't expect long-term leave, more like unpredictable bad days. for oncall i can sign up for fewer rotations and have a backup buddy. i can also shift my review windows out by 24-48h if that helps.
Olivia (People Ops): that sounds reasonable. suggested temporary accommodations we usually offer:
- 2 remote days/week (consistent schedule where possible)
- flexible start/end (core hours 11a–3p)
- reduced oncall frequency (identify buddy coverage)
- formalized check-ins every 2 weeks for 12 weeks to review progress
If you agree, we'll draft a written accommodation memo and route for signatures.
Samir R. (Manager): i can take care of arranging buddy coverage for oncall and will update the rota. also okay with shifting PR review expectations to 48h for Lee's tickets.
Lee W.: appreciate it. one thing — can we keep the details limited to people who need to know? i prefer minimal distribution.
Olivia (People Ops): absolutely. accommodation records are confidential and stored in HR systems. only Samir and assigned HR/EPM will see the doc unless you give permission to share more broadly.
peopleops-bot: Reminder: accommodation meeting scheduled by Olivia for 2026-10-28 10:00 AM with participants: Lee W., Olivia (People Ops), Samir R. (Manager).
Lee W.: confirmed for 10/28. also, can someone confirm whether this impacts eligibility for performance review in the upcoming cycle? i want to make sure this doesn't unintentionally trigger a PIP.
Olivia (People Ops): it should not automatically trigger a PIP. accommodations are intended to enable performance. if there are performance concerns, we handle those separately and take accommodations into account. we'll note the accommodation start date in the employee record so reviewers see context.
Samir R. (Manager): agreed. my plan is to treat this as a temporary adjustment and focus on outcomes for the quarter rather than hours. i'll flag any concerns to people ops before escalating.
Tara P.: Lee, if you decide later you need additional support (e.g., STD or workplace ergonomics), ping me and we can coordinate.
Lee W.: thanks everyone — this feels good. i'll DM the scanned note now and see you at the meeting. :pray:
Olivia (People Ops): thanks, Lee. we'll draft the memo after the meeting and follow up with next steps. :white_check_mark:
_meta: Generated Slack thread about ADA accommodation, flexible schedule, oncall coverage, and manager coordination; confidential HR conversation style; short messages with bot notices and meeting scheduling.
